title: Game Overview
summary: Each round you make decisions across production, logistics, R&D, marketing, HR, and finance. Results are calculated by the game engine.
bullets: Rounds: Trial round is practice; Round 1 starts fresh from default state.
Inputs drive market share, unit sales, costs, and financial statements.
All calculations come from the game engine and game config.

title: Market Demand
summary: Demand is based on base market size, growth, and scenario modifiers, then adjusted by average price elasticity.
bullets: Scenario can raise/lower growth and elasticity.
Demand is computed per region (Americas, Asia, Europe).
Teams compete for market share based on attractiveness score.

title: Market Share
summary: Market share is proportional to attractiveness score per region.
bullets: Attractiveness uses price, quality, features, promotion, CSR, and brand.
Weights differ by region (EU values CSR more; Asia values price more).
Higher score yields higher share of regional demand.

title: Pricing Strategy
summary: Lower prices can boost demand share but reduce margin. Price penalties apply if price is far above baseline.
bullets: Demand shifts with price elasticity relative to the baseline price.
Price affects attractiveness and share, not just revenue.
Use regional baselines and elasticities from the config.

title: Promotion and Marketing
summary: Promotion increases attractiveness; it is region weighted and can be modified by scenarios.
bullets: Promotion % affects promotion score in attractiveness.
High promotion is powerful in EU and US; less in Asia.
Marketing cost is a % of revenue by region.

title: Feature Research
summary: Research hours unlock features that increase attractiveness.
bullets: Feature unlocks are cumulative across rounds (excluding trial).
More features increase demand share via features score.
Industry labels differ (e.g., Oil Refinery Level).

title: Production Planning
summary: Production is limited by factory capacity plus overtime. Outsourcing adds capacity at a premium.
bullets: Capacity per plant is industry-specific.
Overtime increases capacity but increases unit cost.
Total units sold are capped by production + inventory.

title: Outsourcing
summary: Outsourcing provides extra units at a premium cost and uses supplier multipliers.
bullets: Outsourcing cost uses material + labor multiplied by supplier multiplier.
A premium is applied on top of outsourced unit costs.
Outsourcing can be used even if factories have spare capacity.

title: CSR (Corporate Social Responsibility)
summary: What is CSR(Corporate Social Responsibility)
bullets: CSR (Corporate Social Responsibility) measures your company's commitment to ethical and sustainable business practices - think environmental protection, fair labor, and responsible sourcing.

In simple terms: Are you a green company that customers can feel good about supporting? High CSR means eco-friendly suppliers and ethical practices. Low CSR means cheaper materials but a worse brand reputation.

title: Suppliers and CSR
summary: Supplier choice changes unit costs and CSR rating, which affects demand share.
bullets: Supplier multipliers increase material and labor costs.
CSR is weighted into attractiveness (EU highest, Asia lowest).
Higher CSR can improve share even with higher costs.

title: Inventory
summary: Inventory carries over to next round; units sold are capped by production plus inventory.
bullets: Ending inventory = starting inventory + production - units sold.
Inventory can buffer demand spikes or missed production.
Inventory value affects balance sheet.

title: Logistics
summary: Logistics costs depend on shipping routes and tariffs. Priority rules allocate supply.
bullets: Local supply is cheapest; cross-region supply adds tariffs.
Priority order determines which regions get served first.
Logistics costs appear in COGS.

title: Human Resources
summary: HR inputs drive research hours and HR costs.
bullets: Research staff and training increase R&D productivity.
Wages and training costs are operating expenses.
HR spending influences R&D cost directly.

title: Finance
summary: Finance decisions affect cash, debt, share count, and TSR.
bullets: Debt increases cash but adds interest expense.
Dividends reduce cash and affect TSR.
Share issuance and buybacks change shares outstanding.

title: Profit and Loss (P&L)
summary: P&L shows revenue, costs, EBITDA, and net profit by round.
bullets: Revenue = units sold × price per region.
COGS includes materials, labor, logistics, outsourcing.
Operating expenses include R&D, marketing, admin.

title: Balance Sheet
summary: Balance sheet tracks assets, liabilities, and equity.
bullets: Inventory and receivables increase assets.
Debt and payables increase liabilities.
Equity grows with retained earnings.

title: Cash Flow
summary: Cash flow tracks how cash moves across operations, investing, and financing.
bullets: Operating cash flow starts from EBITDA.
Investing includes plant builds and assets.
Financing includes debt and equity actions.

title: Total Shareholder Return (TSR)
summary: TSR measures shareholder return based on share price change and dividends.
bullets: TSR per round uses previous round share price as base.
Dividends add to shareholder return.
Final leaderboard uses compounded TSR across completed rounds.
TSR = (Ending Share Price − Beginning Share Price + Dividends) / Beginning Share Price
Or in percentage:
TSR (%) = [(Ending Price + Dividends) / Beginning Price − 1] × 100

title: Share Price
summary: Share price is derived from EPS and valuation rules in config.
bullets: EPS = net profit / shares outstanding.
Share price = EPS × PE multiple (with bounds).
Price is bounded by floors/guards to avoid extreme swings.

title: Brand Reputation
summary: Brand reputation affects attractiveness as a multiplier.
bullets: Brand bonus scales the final attractiveness score.
Consistent performance improves brand over time.
Scenarios can influence brand effects.

title: Scenarios
summary: Scenarios modify market growth, elasticity, costs, and CSR importance.
bullets: Scenario effects are applied per round.
Demand, costs, and marketing sensitivity can shift.
Admin view shows scenario impact on parameters.

title: Industry Settings
summary: Each industry has different base demand, prices, costs, and capacities.
bullets: Oil uses lower prices and higher volumes.
Automotive uses higher prices and lower volumes.
Industry config is chosen at game creation.

title: Default State
summary: The default state is used for Trial and Round 1 baselines.
bullets: Trial round does not carry into Round 1.
Round 1 starts from default state (round -1).
Subsequent rounds use previous round results.

title: Cumulative return
summary: Total gain/loss of an investment over time as percentage.
bullets: Formula: (Current share price - Original share price) / Original share price × 100%
Shows overall performance regardless of time period.
Does not account for timing of cash flows.

title: P/E
summary: Price-to-Earnings ratio – how much investors pay per dollar of earnings.
bullets: Formula: P/E = Market Price per Share / Earnings per Share (EPS)
High P/E indicates expected future growth.
Low P/E may signal undervaluation or poor prospects.

title: Dividend yield
summary: Annual dividend return relative to current share price.
bullets: Formula: Dividend Yield = (Annual Dividends per Share / Current Share Price) × 100%
Measures income return for shareholders.
Higher yield attractive for income-focused investors.

title: Dividend
summary: Portion of earnings distributed to shareholders.
bullets: Usually quoted as dollars per share or as percentage of share price (yield).
Decided by board of directors.
Reduces retained earnings and company cash.

title: Shares outstanding
summary: Total shares currently held by all shareholders.
bullets: Used to calculate market cap, EPS, etc.
Includes shares held by public and insiders.
Changes with issuances, buybacks, splits.

title: Market capitalization
summary: Total market value of outstanding shares.
bullets: Formula: Market Cap = Shares Outstanding × Current Share Price
Classifies company size (small/mid/large cap).
Fluctuates daily with share price.

title: EBITDA
summary: Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization.
bullets: Formula: EBITDA = Net Income + Interest + Taxes + Depreciation + Amortization
Measures core operating performance.
Ignores financing and accounting decisions.

title: EBIT
summary: Earnings Before Interest and Taxes – operating profit.
bullets: Formula: EBIT = Net Income + Interest + Taxes
Focuses on operational profitability.
Useful for comparing companies with different capital structures.

title: Debt/Equity
summary: Financial leverage ratio – debt vs equity financing.
bullets: Formula: Debt/Equity = Total Liabilities / Shareholders' Equity
Higher ratio = greater financial risk.
Varies widely by industry.

title: ROS
summary: Return on Sales – operating profit margin.
bullets: Formula: ROS = (Operating Profit / Sales) × 100%
Shows profit efficiency per dollar of revenue.
Higher value indicates better cost management.

title: Gearing
summary: Financial leverage – proportion of debt vs equity.
bullets: Commonly expressed as Debt/Equity ratio.
High gearing = higher risk and potential returns.
Depends on industry and economic conditions.

title: Net debt to equity
summary: Leverage after subtracting cash from debt.
bullets: Formula: Net Debt/Equity = (Total Debt - Cash & Equivalents) / Shareholders' Equity
More realistic leverage measure than gross ratio.
Can be negative if cash exceeds debt.

title: ROCE
summary: Return on Capital Employed – capital efficiency.
bullets: Formula: ROCE = EBIT / Capital Employed × 100%
Capital Employed = Equity + Interest-bearing Debt
Higher % = more effective use of capital.

title: Capital Employed
summary: Total capital used in business operations.
bullets: Formula: Capital Employed = Total Assets - Current Liabilities
Also = Equity + Long-term Debt
Base for ROCE calculation.

title: Return on Equity
summary: Profitability from shareholders' investment.
bullets: Formula: ROE = Net Income / Shareholders' Equity × 100%
High ROE attractive but can be inflated by debt.
DuPont formula breaks it into margin × turnover × leverage.

title: EPS
summary: Earnings Per Share – profit per share.
bullets: Formula: EPS = Net Profit / Shares Outstanding
Basic EPS uses weighted average shares.
Key metric for valuation and share price.

title: P&L
summary: Profit and Loss statement (income statement).
bullets: Shows revenue, expenses, and profit over a period.
Key line items: Revenue → COGS → Gross Profit → Operating Expenses → Net Profit.
Used to assess profitability.

title: Receivables
summary: Amounts owed to the company by customers.
bullets: Recorded as current assets on balance sheet.
Includes accounts receivable.
Turnover ratio measures collection efficiency.

title: Payables
summary: Short-term debts owed to suppliers/creditors.
bullets: Recorded as current liabilities.
Includes accounts payable.
High payables can improve cash flow.

title: Share capital
summary: Funds raised by issuing shares to investors.
bullets: Appears in shareholders' equity.
Increases with new share issuances.
Decreases with buybacks.

title: Other restricted equity
summary: Restricted shares issued to insiders/executives.
bullets: Subject to vesting schedules.
Cannot be freely traded.
Often used for employee compensation.

title: Retained earnings
summary: Cumulative profits kept after dividends.
bullets: Formula: Retained Earnings = Beginning RE + Net Income - Dividends
Part of shareholders' equity.
Funds internal growth or debt repayment.

title: Turnover
summary: Rate at which employees leave and are replaced.
bullets: High turnover increases recruitment and training costs.
Low turnover indicates good employee satisfaction.
Calculated as (Number of departures / Average number of employees) × 100%.

title: Efficiency ratio
summary: Measures how effectively a company uses its assets and liabilities.
bullets: Includes asset turnover, receivables turnover, inventory turnover.
Higher ratios = better efficiency.
Varies by industry.

title: Depreciation
summary: Allocation of tangible asset cost over its useful life.
bullets: Reduces taxable income.
Common methods: straight-line, declining balance.
Non-cash expense.

title: Capacity utilisation
summary: Percentage of maximum productive capacity actually used.
bullets: Formula: (Actual output / Potential output) × 100%
High utilisation = efficient use of resources.
Low utilisation may indicate overcapacity.

title: Cost of inventory
summary: Holding/carrying cost of storing inventory.
bullets: Includes storage, insurance, obsolescence.
Typically 20-30% of inventory value per year.
Influences optimal inventory levels.

title: FIFO
summary: First In, First Out inventory method.
bullets: Oldest inventory sold first.
Matches physical flow in most businesses.
Results in higher profits during inflation.

title: LIFO
summary: Last In, First Out inventory method.
bullets: Newest inventory sold first.
Lower profits during inflation (tax benefit).
Not allowed under IFRS.

title: Transfer price
summary: Price charged for transactions between divisions of the same company.
bullets: Used for internal performance evaluation.
Can affect tax liabilities.
Must comply with arm's length principle.

title: Assets
summary: Resources owned by the company.
bullets: Current assets convertible to cash within one year.
Non-current assets used long-term.
Listed on balance sheet.

title: Liability
summary: Legal debts or obligations owed by the company.
bullets: Current liabilities due within one year.
Long-term liabilities due after one year.
Listed on balance sheet.

title: Income taxes
summary: Taxes levied on income/profits.
bullets: Calculated on taxable income.
Deferred taxes arise from timing differences.
Effective tax rate varies by jurisdiction.

title: Administration costs
summary: Overhead/fixed costs not directly tied to production.
bullets: Includes office expenses, salaries, utilities.
Part of operating expenses.
Usually fixed in nature.

title: Loss carry forward
summary: Previous losses offset future taxable income.
bullets: Reduces future tax liability.
Subject to time limits in many jurisdictions.
Valuable for companies with fluctuating profits.

title: Variable administration cost
summary: Admin costs that vary with activity level.
bullets: Example: costs tied to number of plants.
Increases with scale.
Differs from fixed admin costs.

title: CSR
summary: Corporate Social Responsibility – company's impact on society and environment.
bullets: Includes sustainability, ethics, community engagement.
Can improve brand reputation.
Increasingly important for investors.

title: Cash And Cash Equivalents - CCE
summary: Highly liquid assets convertible to cash immediately.
bullets: Includes cash, bank balances, short-term investments.
Key component of liquidity.
Used in current ratio calculation.

title: Decision Science Foundations
summary: AIDL uses a normative approach to decision science, combining mathematical modeling with behavioral insights.
bullets: Deterministic Modeling: Outcomes are calculated via precise economic formulas, not random chance.
Multi-Variable Optimization: Players must balance conflicting KPIs (e.g., Quality vs. Cost).
Longitudinal Study: The simulation tracks decision patterns over multiple fiscal periods.

title: AIDL Proprietary Algorithms
summary: The Lab engine runs on three core AI sub-systems to maintain market realism.
bullets: Attractiveness Scorer: A weighted non-linear function determining consumer preference.
Valuation Engine: A smoothed P/E multiplier system that prevents speculative bubbles.
Reactive AI Rivals: Competitor logic based on game theory primitives (e.g., Trigger Strategies).
